questions.q: The dashed boxes on a slide that hold the title or body text are called:
questions.solution: Placeholders are the pre-formatted containers (title, content, media) defined by the slide layout; text typed into them feeds the Outline view.
questions.shortcut: Presentation-speak: layout defines placeholders; theme defines colours.

questions.q: ARPANET, the precursor of today's Internet, was launched in:
questions.solution: ARPANET went live in 1969 connecting UCLA and Stanford Research Institute, funded by the US Department of Defense.
questions.shortcut: ARPANET 1969 - the 60s birth of the network.

questions.q: The Information Technology Act, which governs cyber activities in India, came into force in:
questions.solution: The IT Act was passed in 2000 (in force from 17 October 2000), based on the UNCITRAL model law; the 2008 amendment added identity theft (66C) and cyber terrorism (66F) provisions.

questions.q: A file saved as .ppsx:
options: Opens directly as a running slide show
questions.solution: The .ppsx 'PowerPoint show' launches straight into the slideshow when double-clicked; to edit it, open PowerPoint first and browse to the file.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

In hot water
questions.solution: Trouble scalds; being 'in hot water' = **in difficulty or disfavour**. Bath, anger and weather options are temperature-literal.
questions.shortcut: Water temperature = trouble scale: hot water = trouble.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Occurrence: double c, double r, **-ence** ending. Occurance/Ocurrance take -ance; Occurence drops an r.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Grandmother's kitchen was the heart of our home. **P:** The aroma of spices filled every corner. **Q:** She kneaded dough before sunrise. **R:** Everyone gathered when the meal bell rang. **S:** No restaurant meal could match her cooking. **6.** We still measure every kitchen by hers.
questions.solution: 'She' needs grandmother (S1) → **Q** opens (morning work). **P** follows (aroma from cooking). **R** brings the family at mealtime. **S** delivers the judgement (no match) before S6. QPRS.
questions.shortcut: Pronoun orphan: She must open; judgement sentence S closes.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Principal congratulated the debate team ___ winning the national championship.
questions.solution: The fixed partnership is **congratulate on**: 'congratulated the team on winning'. The -ing after the blank is exactly what this frame expects.

questions.q: ***The God of Small Things***, winner of the 1997 Booker Prize, was written by —
questions.solution: **Arundhati Roy** won the Booker in **1997** for this Kerala-set debut novel. Kiran Desai won in 2006 for *The Inheritance of Loss*.

questions.q: The Palghat Gap connects which two states?
questions.solution: The **Palghat (Palakkad) Gap** is a low pass in the Western Ghats between the **Nilgiri** and **Anaimalai** hills, linking **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu**. It lets moist winds reach Coimbatore.

questions.q: Bauxite is the chief ore of:
questions.solution: **Bauxite** (hydrated aluminium oxide) is the chief ore of **aluminium**, extracted by electrolysis (Hall–Héroult process).

questions.q: Teflon, used in non-stick cookware, is a polymer of:
questions.solution: **Teflon** is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), made from **tetrafluoroethylene**. Vinyl chloride gives PVC, isoprene gives natural rubber and ethene gives polythene.

questions.q: The average temperature of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday is 37°C and of Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday is 34°C. If the temperature on Monday was 40°C, the temperature on Thursday is:
The average of the squares of the first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.solution:
Sum of squares $= \frac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6} = 385$.
Average $= \frac{385}{10} = 38.5$.

questions.q: A cycle bought for ₹850 is sold for ₹1,020. The profit per cent is:
What is the remainder when $1! + 2! + 3! + \dots + 100!$ is divided by 12?
questions.solution: From $4! = 24$ onwards every term is a multiple of 12. So only $1! + 2! + 3! = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9$ matters. Remainder **9**.

questions.solution: Three rules (places numbered clockwise from the top-left corner, 0-7). Square: 0, 2, 4, 6 — two places clockwise → next **0** (top-left corner). Ring: 7, 6, 5, 4 — one place anticlockwise → next **3** (right-middle). Arrow: down, down-left, left, up-left — 45° clockwise → next **up**. Only one option satisfies all three.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: Four lines from the apex divide the base into 5 parts. Lines through the apex = 4 + 2 = 6; any two form a triangle: C(6, 2) = **15**.

questions.q: How many letters of the English alphabet are there **between D and P** (not counting D and P)?
questions.shortcut: Positions differ by 12; strictly-between is one less.

questions.q: In a queue of 30 people, **A is 9th from the front. If 5 new people join the queue at the front**, what is A's new position from the front?
questions.solution: Every old position shifts back by 5: 9 + 5 = **14th**. (The queue length also grows to 35, but only front-joins affect A's rank.)
questions.shortcut: Front joiners push the tracked person back one-for-one.
